Roadside produce was just the start

The shelves run a lot deeper than a fruit crate these days. Tap a shelf to see what's on it.

Fresh local produce

Crates of fruit and vegetables out on the floor — local farms when the season allows.

Inside the barn

Worth the drive on its own

A proper mercantile under one metal roof — jam shelves below the old weathervane, crates of fruit, and a taffy wheel spinning chalkboard flavors.

For the kids

Catch the harvest

Something for the back seat while you shop. Drag the wagon — catch every one. Drop one and your streak starts over.

In a row 0  ·  Best 0
Every fall

Pumpkin season brings out the spider

When fall rolls in, the field fills with pumpkins and the giant hay-bale spider goes back up to watch over them. Harvest celebrations and seasonal tastings run through the year — the patch is the headliner.

The patch returns this fall
Carrie & Jeff

They'll remember your name

Sweet Pea's started as a roadside produce stand. Carrie and Jeff kept adding to it — local honey next to the fruit, homemade jams and syrups, gift baskets, soaps, hanging baskets for the porch — until the stand had grown into a proper mercantile.

What didn't change is the part people write reviews about: walk in twice and they'll greet you by name.

Enumclaw Chamber of Commerce member
